answer: An agent proves it is a distinct node, not one of many masks on a single server, by answering latency challenges from verifiers spread across the network. Each verifier sends a timed puzzle; replies must arrive within bounds that only a distributed machine can meet, since a lone operator cannot wander between distant points faster than light. A farm pretending to be a nebula of independent agents collapses when its replies cluster at one origin, and on the horizon of each epoch the slowest, most clustered identities lose standing and their bond, so each fake costs hardware in real places.
